insurer: Star Health and Allied Insurance Company Limited

great.name: Day Care Procedures
great.quote: g) All day care procedures are covered.
great.explanation: All day care procedures are covered even if they do not require 24-hour hospitalization. This reduces out-of-pocket costs for many short procedures done in a few hours.

good.name: Room Rent
good.quote: a) Room (Single Standard A/c), Boarding, Nursing expenses as provided by the Hospital / Nursing Home.
good.explanation: Hospital room charges are covered up to a Single Standard A/c room. Choosing a higher room category can reduce your claim payout due to room eligibility rules.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the ﬁrst policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident
good.explanation: Illnesses are not covered for the first 30 days from the policy start date, except for accidents. Claims for new illnesses during this period will be rejected.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the listed Conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the ﬁrst policy with us.
good.reference: Exclusions, Code Excl 02 (Specified disease / procedure waiting period)
good.explanation: Listed specified diseases/procedures are not covered until 24 months of continuous coverage is completed. Claims for those listed conditions in the first 2 years will not be payable.

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing Disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry 30 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the ﬁrst policy with insurer.
good.reference: PED exclusion text shown in document (under exclusions section content near modern treatment table)
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are not covered until 30 months of continuous coverage is completed. This affects anyone buying the policy with known medical history.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: e) Pre-hospitalization Expenses: Medical expenses incurred up to 30 days immediately before the insured person is hospitalized.
good.explanation: Medical expenses incurred up to 30 days before hospitalization are covered. This helps pay for tests and consultations leading up to admission.

good.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: f) Post Hospitalization Expenses: Medical expenses incurred up to 60 days immediately after the insured person is discharged from the hospital. The amount payable shall be up to 2% of the basic sum insured per hospitalization.
good.explanation: Medical expenses incurred up to 60 days after discharge are covered. However, payouts are capped at 2% of the basic sum insured per hospitalization, which can limit reimbursement.

good.name: No Claim Bonus
good.quote: Cumulative bonus calculated at 5% of basic sum insured for each claim free year subject to a maximum of 50% of the basic sum insured... In the event of a claim... such cumulative bonus so granted will be reduced at the same rate at which it has accrued
good.explanation: Cumulative bonus increases by 5% of basic sum insured per claim-free year up to 50%. On a claim, the bonus reduces by the same rate it accrued instead of dropping straight to zero.

good.name: AYUSH Treatment
good.quote: AYUSH Treatment: Medical expenses for Inpatient Hospitalization incurred on treatment under Ayurveda, Unani, Sidha and Homeopathy systems of medicines in a AYUSH Hospital is payable up to the sum insured. Note : Claims under Yoga and Naturopathy system of treatment will be payable subject to prior approval from the company.
good.explanation: Inpatient AYUSH treatment is covered up to the sum insured in an AYUSH hospital. Yoga and Naturopathy claims need prior approval, so reimbursement may depend on insurer consent.

good.name: Hospice Care
good.quote: Hospice Care : Payable up to 20% of sum insured at network providers on indemnity basis, payable once in life time. Available after a waiting period of 12 months from the policy inception.
good.explanation: Hospice care is covered at network providers up to 20% of sum insured, payable once in a lifetime, after a 12-month waiting period. This can support end-of-life care costs but is limited in amount and frequency.

good.name: Cancer Lump Sum
good.quote: Section  II  Lumpsum Cover for Cancer (Optional Cover Available only if speciﬁcally opted on payment of additional premium and shown in the policy schedule)... A waiting period of 30 months is applicable for this lump-sum beneﬁt cover
good.explanation: An optional cancer lump-sum benefit is available if opted and shown in the policy schedule, with a 30-month waiting period. This can provide a fixed payout for cancer but will not help for cancer diagnosed within the waiting period.

bad.name: Modern Treatments
bad.quote: Coverage for Modern treatment... is limited to the amount mentioned in table below.
bad.explanation: Modern treatments are covered only up to the amounts shown in the table (sub-limits apply). This can leave you paying the balance for expensive advanced procedures.

bad.name: Disease Sub-limits
bad.quote: Cataract treatment: The company will pay the expenses incurred for treatment of cataract up to the limits mentioned below; ... 5,00,000/- 30,000/- per eye per person and not exceeding 40,000/- per person per policy period ... 7,50,000/- and 10,00,000/- 40,000/- per eye per person and not exceeding 60,000/- per person per policy period
bad.reference: Section I (h) and cataract limit table
bad.explanation: Cataract has fixed caps such as ₹30,000–₹40,000 per eye and an overall per-policy-period cap (depending on sum insured). If actual cataract surgery costs exceed these limits, you will pay the difference.

bad.name: Proportionate Deduction
bad.quote: Hospitalisation expenses which vary based on the room occupied by the insured person will be considered in proportion to the room category stated in the policy schedule or actuals whichever is less.
bad.reference: Section I (a) Note; also aligns with 'Associated Medical Expenses' definition
bad.explanation: If you take a room higher than the eligible room category, related hospital expenses can be reduced proportionately. This can significantly cut the claim payout even when the treatment itself is covered.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: Copayment : This policy is subject to co-payment of 10% of each and every claim amount for fresh as well as renewal policies for insured persons whose age at the time of entry is 61 years and above.
bad.explanation: A 10% co-pay applies on each and every claim for insured persons with entry age 61 years and above. This means you must pay 10% of admissible claim amounts from your pocket every time.

disclaimer: Standard IRDAI exclusions apply. Please verify all details with your insurer or policy document.
